Formulation
Patient presents with a possible flare-up of eczema, characterized by itchy and sore skin, affecting daily activities, sleep, and concentration at work. Predisposing factor: history of eczema. No immediate precipitating or perpetuating factors identified, but environmental allergens may play a role. No protective factors explicitly stated beyond motivation to seek treatment.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Itchy and sore skin
- Patient Goal(s): Relief from itchiness and soreness, improved sleep and function at work
- Clinical Goal(s): Manage flare-up of eczema
- Actions (Patient): Use prescribed steroids, emollients, and antihistamines; maintain a trigger diary
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe stronger topical steroids and antihistamines; recommend follow-up if no improvement

Secondary Problem: Not applicable

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Use of medications, diary for triggers
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increase in itchiness, spread to new areas
- Coping Strategies: Using medications as prescribed, identifying triggers
